Overall good cam While I did end up looking elsewhere and bought another cam that was more satisfactory with additional useful features, this cam is still very good.

It has a decent recording time (didn’t keep track but it was a few hours) and the picture quality is good, even while in motion.

The only drawback for me is I found it tricky at times to tell if it was actually recording or not.
While I did get the hang of it, there were times I wasn’t sure it was actually recording until I removed the memory card and was able to confirm whether or not that was the case.
Almost perfect, but not quite This is a great body cam.
I had bought 2 previous ones from other companies, but while sufficient for certain purposes, I right away realized they fell short in other crucial areas.

Most importantly to me, the pros to this one is the lengthy battery life, night vision/IR, motion stability, loop recording, easy to tell if it’s actually recording, ability to set date/time on the cam itself without having to go thru a USB cord to a computer, and a screen to view the footage without having to put the memory card in a computer or device to view it.

However, the downsides which prevent this from being perfect/5* for me are these: mostly the fact that the clip/s, even the large sturdy one, isn’t sufficient in length and heft to enable the cam to remain in the right position/angle, as the weight of the cam pulls the clip down and I’m left with footage facing towards the ground/floor, and not at the higher level I need it to catch (a solution is to clip it horizontally where it stays out much better, only issue is the footage is now in portrait and not landscape).
Other lesser cons are the clip/s lack the ability to rotate, the product pic does indicate otherwise but such is not the case, at least with the clips packaged with my cam.

Also, the date/time is so tiny as to be unreadable when viewing footage on the cam, so when there’s a part I want to review, I’m unable to just skip to the time it happened and instead have to FF until I see it.
Lastly, while it’s good that the clip stays firmly and securely in place, it’s a nightmare to remove!
Despite these issues, overall this is a great cam and I don’t feel the need to look further for another one.
Do wish tho that there was the option of ordering replacement clips, just in case it should get damaged or accidentally misplaced.

Works great after changing modes to MBIM For those using this MC7455 card in a Mini-PCIe to USB adapter, if you have issues with it passing data reliably, this information is for you.

* This MC7455 card can operate in two different interface modes: QMI or MBIM
* The card ships by default from SierraWireless in QMI mode, but most OS's ( Windows and Linux confirmed ) work much better with MBIM mode.
* While in QMI mode, I was able to establish a network connection, but outbound traffic basically didn't work for anything more than 'ping'.

To overcome this, you need to connect to the Modem's COM port for AT commands.
Note that there are multiple COM ports assigned to the card, only one will work for AT commands.
This is typically the highest COM port number which is associated with the card.

You can find the right COM port by trial and error.. it won't hurt anything if you hit the wrong one.

NOTE: Proceeding below uses administrative config functions, which if not set properly can render the card useless.

While I have completed this successfully on two cards and have not had any issues, proceed at your own risk.

In Windows, I recommend downloading 'putty'.

When you run it, select 'Serial' under 'Connection type:', then change the 'Serial line' parameter to COM# (where # is the COM port you want to test), then leave the 'Speed' value set to 9600 and click 'Open'

In Linux, install 'screen', then use the command as follows:
# mmcli -m 0| grep ports
-- Look for the 'ttyUSB#' port associated with (at)
# screen /dev/ttyUSB2 9600
-- Note that 'ttyUSB2' is the port assigned to the (at) command interface.

Once connected to the port, you can proceed as follows:
1: Type the following command and press Enter (you will not see the letters as you type them):
ate1
- This turns on 'echo', meaning after this line is entered, you will see the keys you type as you type them.

2: Type the following and press Enter:
ati
- This should show the model, firmware and other details for the modem.

3: Type the following and press Enter:
at!

entercnd="A710"
- This enabled administration configuration commands

4: Type the following and press Enter:
at!

usbcomp=1,1,1009
- This changes the modem to MBIM mode

5: Type the following and press Enter:
at!

reset
- This resets the modem so it will reboot into MBIM mode

At this point, if using putty, it will likely complain of a disconnection and close out.

If using 'screen' in Linux, press:
Ctrl-a followed by k, then answer 'Yes' to kill this window.

Once the modem finishes its restart, you should be able to fully utilize the MC7455 for a solid, stable and FAST internet connection ( all other conditions being favorable, of course ).

I let it sit for a while thinking it was just a coincidence, then I turned it back on and got the same thing.
I turned it off again, took the card out, then turned it back on and luckily it still works.
It DID, however, erase my saves during this ordeal.

Luckily I have cloud saves enabled and was able to restore my save state.

I had done some research on this item prior to purchasing it for my Switch, and it seems to have some solid reviews.
Having said that, the product that I personally received straight from Amazon seems to be a cheap knock-off of the real thing.

Before today, I didn't know that "fake" SD cards were a thing.

The packaging seemed a bit "off" when it arrived in the mail.
The front and back of the cardboard packaging was not lined up (pictured), and the imprints of the company logo are not lined up with the ink on the actual packaging.
Looking at the plastic shell that it's in, you can tell that it wasn't pressed in a factory like other SD card holders.
The last indicator, one that I didn't get a picture of before I opened it, was that the area over the SD card adaptor was "bulged out" and the lining around it was crinkled.

You can still kind of tell from the fourth picture I included above - the top was like that before I opened it.

I reached out to Amazon customer service about the issue, but they did not assist me other than offering a refund without having to return the original item.

Due to their response to my claim, I don't think they will be looking into this issue further and as a result, you run the risk of damaging your Switch or losing your save states by purchasing this item.
I'm sure some of this product are the real deal, but obviously there are some fakes mixed in with their shipments.

Very disappointing.

Update: Despite the agent I chatted with claiming he forwarded it to someone higher up and that they would be in touch with me to resolve the issue due to it almost bricking my system, no one ever contacted me.

i9-10980XE (9980xe) (7980xe) Looks like Amazon incorrectly labeled this item the 10920x which is only a 12 core cpu.

I managed to snag one off of Newegg.
The 10980xe is an 18 core monster that is just a revision from the 7980xe and the 9980xe.
This cpu still drops into x299 boards and behaves almost identically to the 7980xe and 9980xe with the exception of slightly higher stock clocks.

The major selling point is the price with a massive 50% off of the original MSRP of the 9980xe.

The skylake-x mesh architecture suffers compared to coffeelake's(9900k) ringbus in gaming applications.
You will actually lose performance in gaming compared to a 9900k.

The 10980xe does bring more cores along with the features that come with the x299 platform making it a great workstation.

I consider the 18 core 10980xe a good core count in between the 12 from the 3900x and the 24 from threadripper 3.
At the time of writing, I cannot consider the 3950x despite its incredible performance because of how unavailable they are.
As of now, the 3950x is $999.99 on Newegg, $899 on B and H photo, $900-$1000 on ebay, and $929 from sellers on Amazon.

Best Buy is the only one honoring the $749.00 MSRP...

The overclocking headroom on the 10980xe is incredible.
With ambient water cooling(360 clc) I can hit 5ghz across all 18 cores.
The heat is almost unmanageable at the moment for me so I will be looking into a custom loop in the future.
As always with overclocking, your results may vary.

The product info says these are machine washable, as long as you remove the electronics obviously.
They are not, and this bold faced lie is why this product almost got 2 stars instead of 3.
That right there is false advertising, folks.
They may remove the picture after I leave this review, but it was there when I posted this.

See my review pictures.

There is no noise cancelling for the headphones.
Maybe they meant for the mic in call mode, but I took no calls on these, so I didn't rate it.
But no these are just normal headphones and not noise cancelling.
The sounds quality is surprisingly good honestly.

Like some other reviewers, I use these for bedtime ASMR or moderation audio files, and they are quality enough to work for this purpose.

They posted over Bluetooth no problem at all, first time.
However the operation of the device is where I have up nitpick.
First of all, you should know that to skip a track you press forward or back and to adjust the volume, you hold forward or back.
You read that right, and this is objectively wrong.
Volume is something you want to adjust precisely, so a button push to lower or raise the volume 1 point would be the best implementation.
Holding the buttons down should be for skipping tracks, as it's pretty clear when a new track is playing-- this does not require precision.

It gets one star off for this insane control scheme.

And lastly, remember when I said that these are great for bedtime?
That was a half-truth.
When the headphones turn on, pair, unpair, or turn off, a super loud computer voice says "POWER ON," "PAIRING," "POWER OFF," etc.
This is the second thing that someone must have been insane to implement considering this is a specialty product for sleep / nightime.
If the unit shuts off while you are asleep, or loses it's Bluetooth connection, it will wake you up, so keep that in mind.

There is no way to turn this voice off or make it quieter that I am aware of, it's not mentioned in the included instructions.

Only other weird thing is when it pairs, it always sets the the volume to a specific and pretty loud volume, but I couldn't tell if that was the player or the headphones.

Pro-tip: adjust the playback volume on your device, not on these headphones awful control interface.

I like them enough to keep them, I'm not retuning mine and I use them still, but my advice is to search for a set without all of these horrible design oversights.

Great non-cloud based camera This is a great camera.

I tried a few features and they have all worked fine for me.

Motion detection: The motion detection is pretty sensitive.
Even when reducing the sensitivity threshold to a very low value, it picks up small things like rain, or moving plants with the wind.
However, you can select a rectangular region of interest to trigger.
I ended up making a very small region of interest in a small location where I'm guaranteed to have no swaying plants, and no rain dripping from rain gutters.

I only wish we could create more than one region of interest for the motion detector for outdoor environments with lots of activity.

The saving to a local FTP server also works fine as well.

I had to create a connection without a certificate (also make sure your firewalls will accept the traffic from this camera).

The email feature works fine.

However, I noticed that when I click test, sometimes the software says the test failed, even though it actually succeeded (and I receive an email).

I like the alarm feature.

It makes it very easy to review videos, if you set the motion detection right.

The video quality is decent.
I can see what I need.
You can select between two modes, SD and HD.

I find that SD is generally enough for me.

I never use the pan tilt and zoom feature after setting it up.
It is useful for setup, but if you have motion detection setup on a region of interest, you'll generally not want to move it.

Still this is very useful to have.

There is one feature I have not tested yet.
At some point, my SD card will run out of space.
The camera should overwrite old videos.

However, I have not run out of enough space to comment on that.

Overall, if you want an easy to setup camera that does not connect to any cloud services, this is a great camera.
However, be prepare for some manual setup and tweaking.

Best laptop for the money I was looking to upgrade from my 2 yr old LG gram to something with more power for solidworks.

This model seemed to fit the bill and had that Microsoft Surface look to it.

First thing I did upon receiving the laptop was a windows reset and then I popped in 64 gb of ram.

Removal of the back cover was quite easy to do and the memory was easy to access.

Then i removed most of the microsoft bloat (using Tron) and uninstalled most of the MSI programs.
The Laptop was fast but still had some minor hiccups like my bluetooth disappearing until i rebooted the laptop.
So i decided to create a USB image of win 10 and then reformat and reinstall everything from scratch.

Once I re-installed only the essential MSI utility programs and drivers.

Laptop gets about 8 hours of battery use with surfing the web and office programs.
With solidworks and PCNB CAD apps it gets about 5-6 hours.

There are still some issues with the Creator program that controls the laptop such as apps that don't switch over to integrated as they should even though you specify them to, but other than that this is a smoking deal.

The Video Reviews on Youtube are a touch misleading.
Prerequisite: I daily drive Galaxy Buds, have tried Airpods, Airpods Pro and had a couple pairs of (2017) Anker SoundCore earbuds.

I also use AKG K7XX's as my main over the ear headphones.

My review will focus mostly on sound quality, because build quality is just what you would expect from $50 earbuds: cheap plastics, but a solid build overall.

Once they're in your ears, it doesn't make much of a difference.
They stick out of my ears more than I expected.
The case is bigger than I expected, I'm not a fan of the shiny, fingerprint-magnet top of the case, and I would have preferred USB-C.

But for $50 bucks, it's good enough, and NOT bad.

Now, the first and most important thing with sound quality: If you like the sound signature of Beats headphones, you'll love these.

They have INCREDIBLE fullness and reverberation to the bass.
It seriously shocked me when I firs turned on a song.
If you love bass, these are hands down the best value for money I've come across.
They blow my Galaxy buds out of the water and Airpods/Pro don't come close, either.
THAT SAID, the bass isn't incredibly detailed.
It's definitely not muddy, but as I mentioned before, there's a lottt of reverberation.
You can FEEL the bass.
It was by FAR the main focus when the engineers designed these things.
And unfortunately, I haven't found a way to tone it down.

It's not my cup of tea, though if I were going for a run or working out, I MIGHT grab these over my Galaxy Buds, just for that extra pump.

That said, the mids are pretty dry.
Listening to voices in podcasts or Youtube videos is actually great, but there's no dynamism to the mids.
They're just there.
Clean and clear on their own, but they easily get lost in the lows and highs when listening to music.
But just voices alone, for podcasts, they're great, and you won't notice the lackluster mids in that case.

With music, they definitely left me wanting for more.

On to the highs: I'm not a fan of sharp highs.
Highs for me can easily be overdone and too sharp, and in this case, they are.
They're very airy, a touch tinny, and pushed forward enough to the point where if I had an EQ I'd dial them down 3+dB.
They're once again not very dynamic, very strong, and easily overpower the mids.

They ARE somewhat detailed, but the tinny-ness and strong presence leave me really wishing I could use an EQ to drop them and raise the mids.

Overall, I'd give sound quality a C+

Soundstage is pretty wide for earbuds, and they're loud enough that I was afraid to turn them to max volume for fear of breaking my eardrums (lol).

The Airpods Pro are MUCH more dynamic, the Galaxy Buds are much more well rounded, and though lacking in bass, do a much better job in every other area.

But they're anywhere from 2-5x as expensive.

Every video review I saw RAVED about these as the best earbuds under $100.
And they MIGHT be right...

But I'd be surprised.

In Conclusion:
I bought these for my wife, but I wish I would have jumped on the SoundCore Liberty Air 2's when they were $110 instead.
I think SoundCore does a better job overall with balance and bass, and the pair I have only cost $26 almost 3 years ago, so I'm sure they've come a long way since then.
I'd recommend checking out what they have in your price range over these, unless ALL you're after is MAD BUMPING bass.

The unit also includes a flip cover/stand and power adaptor similar to that commonly found packaged with modern smartphones.
The flip cover/stand is loose fitting and is attached to the device by magnets located within both the monitor and the screen.
The adherence of the cover to the monitor leaves you wanting something more sturdy, such as a washable adhesive.
The monitor also includes a screen protector.

Using the utmost care, a roll of tape and a flat plastic card, I still received bubbles underneath the protector.

Using a 26800mAh portable battery bank, the monitor works well with Nintendo Switch, and Samsung Dex off of a Galaxy S10+, 512 GB, 8GB ram.

Audio from the monitor's 2 speakers is the quality better than an Amazon Echo (gen 3) and google home mini.
I have not had much time playing music on it, but I would like to think it is on par with an S10+, below a Tab S6 speakers.

As a portable device, the speakers work well for playing games and watching videos.

To utilize the device with my laptop (HP Spectre X360 15.6, intel i7-8705G CPU w/ AMD Radeon RX Vega, 16gb ram) I would have to plug the USB-C to USB-C first to power the portable monitor, then if I felt like charging the laptop I could plug in the (laptop) power adapter.
If you are using this method, be sure to plug into the correct port of the monitor, as one can supply power and video, while another supplies only power.

If the connection is attempted with the laptop plugged in, the monitor is not recognized and does not receive any power to turn on.

Currently using the portable monitor in conjunction with my desktop computer to stream videos while working/gaming.
The video seems dull, but brightness is only set at 65 with the included screen protector.

My desktop computer specs: with Intel i7-6800k 3.4GHz CPU, 32 GB ram, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (2 in SLI).

Overall, the metallic exterior casing of the monitor feels premium and the lack of an internal batter assist in keeping the weight of the device to an acceptable weight for most people to carry around.
The flip cover/stand works for the device because of the portable nature but leaves you wanting something more in the way it is secured to the monitor for transport.
Image quality is smooth, moving through the built-in menu takes some getting used to and can be considered intuitive to average computer users.

Not good for solid shielded Cat6a I don't need Cat6A speeds but I do like to have shielding in the house because I never know what interference I'll get in the walls and cables...
I was using the Cable Matters Cat6a Tool Free terminators and love them.
But I decided to try the Ubiquiti UAP-AC-PRO AP's so I could manage everything in one location and view usages...
But after receiving those I found that they were not designed well for those large connectors and there was no way to fit them into the ethernet port on the back.
But I could squeeze in a normal terminated ethernet cable.
So I ordered these and a Klein VDV226-110.. mistake number one.

As I am using Cat6a F/UTP it is some thick stuff and the Klein will not crimp the rear ground shield, These are not pull through so you have to try and fiddle the cable to the correct standard and length while removing the foil and then get the cable to fit into a tiny guide and into the connector, NOT easy on the F/UTP shielded sold strand cable.
Went through three connectors trying to do that.
The little plastic guide for these connectors expands in the middle and wont hold the individual strands in a good order to insert into the connectors.
Another problem I had was after crimping the connectors I didn't have a good way to compress the ground/shield support so I couldn't get the boot on all the way.
Then when I twisted the cable to get it to fit into the Ubiquity AP, the ethernet cable strand would twist away from the internal pin connection, causing the cable to go bad...
I could straighten it out, it would work, twist it, and fail.
Definitely not good for solid cable and tight spaces.

These might be ok using a tool like the AMPCOM One-step RJ45 Ratcheting Crimper that will also crimp the ground/shield support and stranded cable but otherwise don't buy this for solid shielded cable.
I am really disappointed in these for the price and plastic quality.

Satisfied after installation Installation can be troublesome if you block access by MAC addresses to your network.

On your home network, disable MAC access, review clients on your network, add the repeater's MAC (and/or devices) then re enable MAC address restrictions.

The MAC printed on the sticker attached to the product is NOT the MAC the repeater used to connect to my home network.

Devices connecting thru the repeater will NOT use their MAC address-they use the manufacturer's MAC prefixed to the device's MAC address.

Again - On your home network, disable MAC access, review clients on your network, add the repeater's MAC (and/or devices) then re enable MAC address restrictions.

Range seems to be adequate.

Works well with 2 Roku TVs in upstairs bedrooms with repeater located in stairwell and home network router in basement.

Don't waste your time with WPS.
Remember- access the repeater's interface on the IP address of the repeater.

Better yet plug into the Ethernet port and configure the repeater from there.

Once you get past installation I think you will be satisfied.

Has saved my Chromebook from falls time and time again!
I bought this case as soon as I got my Acer Chromebook 11 C740-C4PE (fits great with this model!)
Soon after, THUMP!
WHUMP!
Every time my Chromebook has slid off my bed, I've tentatively cracked it open, a lump in the pit of my stomach, only to find it running like nothing even happened.
The case itself is near-indestructible.
A year to the day (and countless 2 foot falls) a tiny bit of corner has finally chipped off, but it still fits fine.
Speaking of fit, this case snaps on securely.

You won't find it popping off at random, inopportune moments, yet it detaches easily enough if you apply enough pressure to the right area.
Whoever wrote in their review that the colored cases "make it look like a children's toy" are, at best, incredibly insecure, or suffering from some severe visual aesthetic disability.
My purple case, especially when attached to my black C. book, makes it look chic, unique, and subtly yet elegantly feminine.
In study groups or meetings, where everyone else's is grey or black, nobody's going to accidentally grab your laptop (nor vice-versa) and it's easy to find.

The size and weight difference is negligible.
The only "con" is true for all these types of cases.
If liquid is spilled, especially something sticky, remove the case immediately.
Otherwise, you have liquid stuck between the case and the laptop -- seeping into important components.
Imagine Mountain Dew drying on your CPU fan, congealing into a viscous, sticky, gel-like substance.
The removal of such things (if your laptop survives!)

demands either a high repairman's fee -- if they don't deem it too disgusting to work on -- or arduous component disassembly and grueling -- albeit delicate -- cleaning.
In summary, worth every penny!

Great PoE Switch at a great value The Aumox PoE switch is a great value.
I had been looking for a small PoE switch to replace the various POE injectors I am using for my access points.
When I first opened the package, I was impressed by the small size of the switch.
The power brick is about the same size as the switch, so I just used some dual-lock fastener to put the power brick on top of the switch to help with a cleaner installation.

Granted it would look even better if the power brick was just a little bit smaller.

It was important that the switch had gigabit to maximize the AC wireless from my Access points.
The Aumox provides a gigabit speeds.
I have the switch powering 3 Ubiquiti AP ACPro.

What is great is that this switch is almost the price of 1 their PoE injector, which again is great especially if you need to have more than 1 AP.

The Aumox quickly powered on the access points without any issues.
I ran various speed tests and I was getting my advertised speed of 250/15Mbps on internet speed tests via the switch.

No difference in speeds between using an injector and moving to the Aumox.

I plugged my laptop directly to the Aumox and performed a file transfer to another device on my other switch and confirmed getting speeds of 112MB/s which is approximately 0.896gbps.

This is impressive considering the overhead and that I had my APs also plugged into the switch.

Another important item for me on a switch is that it is fanless with quiet operation.

I know with POE switches they can get warm, however, after using my switch it seems to be passively cooled and feels the same temperature as my other devices.

Overall the switch seems sturdy with a good build quality.
It’s a great value for the price and I highly recommend it to anyone needing a POE switch for their access points.

Maybe the BEST DisplayLink dock. (at this price) This dock is featured on the front page of the official DisplayLink website, and headlines a 2018 pamphlet alongside wireless VR.
It's probably featured elsewhere on DisplayLink's website for good reason: it's probably the best solution a home user can get as a TRULY universal dock.
And at a good hundred dollars less than other USB-C docks with Power Delivery.
It's worked with most everything I've plugged it into, even older USB 2 devices.

Just remember that you HAVE to install software from DisplayLink for this to work.
Also there are some hell devices that just won't work, no matter how excellent the DisplayLink standard is for universal compatibility.
An old Nexbit Robin I tried using just refused to work.
Had the software installed and all set up just like other phones I tried this on...no dice.
I guess Nexbit was too garbage to implement the USB standard correctly, as that is the LITERAL only way it would fail to connect right.
Last thing that wouldn't work is super-old systems; DisplayLink runs off of the CPU and can get intensive to run.
So make sure to test it within the return window with everything you want to connect it to!
That said, there isn't another dock at this price that supports DisplayLink and Power Delivery through USB-C.
Get it!

When I plugged it in, something happened to my PC in regards to the startup page when turning the system on.
It wouldn't load past the Gigabyte Screen, and BIOS couldn't solve the issue.

After 8 hours of digging, a friend and I found a way to get the PC to boot with the card (we didn't know it was the card at the time).
Several days later, I updated my Radeon RX 5700 driver and the PC automatically restarted and refused to boot.
It was very frustrating, and it also happened several other times (all with other drivers in the system) after I rebooted the PC back to before updating the driver.
We had done a speed/practice build of the same PC a week earlier-without the Wifi Card due to late shipping.

So, I went ahead and updated the drivers and waited for the boot error, turned off the PC and unplugged the Wifi Card, and turned it back on.
Voila, it worked.
For some reason, the card didn't like the AMD build of my PC.
It did have all of it's driver installed, so there was no reason for the strange issue.

It was easy to install, got great signal, but the product itself had major problems while working inside the PC-earning it a 2 rating.
I hope this troubleshoot helps and warns people who are considering on buying this product.

Major Software Flaws Sure, it's on the lower end of the Thunderbolt 3 dock pricing spectrum - but it's still $200 and for that much I expect a product that does what it's supposed to do without having to think about it.
It's a dock.
It should just sit there and connect my computer to things.
It does not.

Here are some of the problems I've experienced since purchasing this dock about 1 month ago (none have been resolved despite dealing with CalDigit tech support and going to the trouble of installing 3rd party beta drivers):
• First and foremost, when my computer goes to sleep with the ethernet cable plugged into the dock it brings my entire LAN down with it.
The whole house and anything connected to WiFi included.

This is completely unacceptable and makes one of the primary uses for me (hardwired network connection) very frustrating to use.
• When waking my computer from sleep the external display (connected via DisplayPort) is not recognized about 75% of the time.
I have to unplug the thunderbolt cable and plug it back in.
Then wait.
Then unplug it again and wait.
Then plug it back in.
This is not why I bought a dock.

If I wanted to plug and unplug cables all day long I would have saved my $200 and bought adapters.
• There's an obnoxious blue light on the front of this dock that can not be turned off.

If you plan to work past sunset you'll have to find some black electrical tape like I did.
• There's no micro SD card slot, only standard SD.
I knew this before purchasing but really should have thought more about it because those micro->standard adapters are yet another step I have to go through when I want to get something done.

If it weren't for the other issues I probably wouldn't mind that much, but it's just one more annoyance I have with this dock.
That's all I can think of at the moment.
When something else goes wrong I'll try to remember to update this review.

Great solution for music while lap swimming!
I purchased these to replace a waterproof mp3 with the in-ear earbuds for lap swimming.
I tried two of the most highly rated in-ear earbuds, but never was able to get them to work comfortably and consistently with water leaking into my ear and cutting off the sound.
The Aftershoks are a much better solution for swimming.

They stay in place (without swim cap) in turns and the sound is very good and consistent underwater and are very comfortable to wear.

I use these primarily for swimming and since Bluetooth does not work underwater, having the built in MP3 player is the only real way to get music in the pool unless you want to swim with wired earbuds and your smart phone.
The sound quality is good with or without the ear plugs.
With the ear plugs I did not notice much of a difference between pool and normal mode.
Without the ear plugs, the sound is much more bassy and would recommend pool mode.
Whether or not to use ear plugs is mostly personal preference on sound and comfort.
I am on the fence.

One complaint was would be nice if the volume could get louder, but the volume is definitely adequate for lap swimming.

Copying music over was straight forward, but formats are limited, so you may have to convert some music files (that are not format protected) to acceptable file types.

Of course, you have to own the songs and can’t just download from one of the subscription music services.

While the xtrainerz are the best music delivery device for swimming and would highly recommend them, I am sticking with the in-ear wireless ear buds and my smartphone for non-water activities as the sound quality is superior and I have more options for music.

Decent USB Hub however outdated as a USB Miner hub Ok I bought this unit about a year ago and have been using it ever since so figured with a year use I will have decent enough  feedback for a review.
First off since it's being advertised as a usb mining hub.
With the current miners on the market in 2019, this hub is NOT really designed to handle them.
The Sapphire Block Erupter back in 2013 and  Bitmain's Antminer U1 for example were ideal for this hub.
However today's USB miners being Gekkoscience Newpacs and Futurebit's Moonlander 2 are not ideal.
As they need minimum 2.5 to 3 amps per port to run these miners correctly.
And this hub does not deliver if you are going to use more than 3 of any of these types of usb miners.
I currently have 3 Moonlander 2's running on this hub and that is maxing the hubs usage.

If I put a 4th Moonlander on this hub then it starts resetting the Asic's due to power issues.

With Newpacs it is worse.
You can only run 2 newpacs on this hub.

Anything more than that and you will run into power issues for the asic miners.

So final break down on what I gave it 3 stars.
Mainly the build of the unit and quality as it is pretty solid and has been dependable for what I've used it for.
I deducted 2 stars for  1:  Advertising is outdated.
This product is no longer suited for usb miners.
It is now more of a data hub / charging station only.
And 2: which backs up the outdated advertising is not being able to run more than 2 (newpacs) or 3 (moonlanders) usb miners on this hub.

Comfortable, clear sounding earbuds In recently lost my longtime earbuds that I have been using for two years.

Saw these on sale and thought I'd give them a go.
Let's break this review into categories; sound, ergonomics, connectivity, and usability

I'll start with,
Ergonomics:
These are tiny, and super lightweight.

I used the large ear tips, and they feel like they are in there to stay, no falling out or anything like that.
I kind of wish they went in a little deeper though.

I find myself pushing them in trying to get a better seal in my ear.
I was able to sit through hours of watching the Witcher on my IPad very comfortably though.
Other than wishing they were a little deeper, my only other complaint is that the hard plastic body, gets uncomfortable if you push them all the way in, but I think that would be an issue with any earbuds with this design.

Usability:
I'm not a fan of the button controls, they "click" which is a bit uncomfortable in the ear.
The aside of that is that there are no accidental button presses.

Once you learn what button combination does what it's fairly intuitive (except volume control) triple clicking on an earbuds sucks, and often times results in a track change.
But pausing Netflix when walking away from the iPad or when someone is talking to you works well.
Also the charging case is fun to play with, satisfying clamp on the lid.
The earbuds are definitely in there and will not easily fall out.

I typically have to use a thumbnail to get them out.

Connectivity:
Seems great overall, but I have had times where (in the first day) the right earbud will lose sound for a quick half second.
It's very jarring when it happens.
I was Within 2- 3 feet of the iPad when this happened.

I can listen to them in different rooms and overall connectivity to my IPad pro, and my Moto z2 force seemed good
Speaking of which, these can only connect to one device at a time.

You have to manually disconnect to change devices, not a deal breaker for me.
There are significant delays in audio from YouTube, and more pressingly gaming.
Played call of duty mobile...

Sound comes a bit after the gun shot.

SOUND
Very clear sound, these are great for watching videos and all the words are super clear.
The highs are absolutely perfect....
Maybe I got a defective pair though, because other reviews mention bass, there is none on the pair I received, bass was completely absent.

I tried Spotify, Netflix the epic orchestral track of the Witcher
sounds awesome, just sans bass.
This may be the deal breaker for me.
I turned them up tried some bass heavy tracks, and nothing.

Again, they are very clear, but don't expect to hear the bass drop.
Outside of that one gripe I actually really dig these, I cannot recommend them with that flaw though, I used the largest eartips to try and hear that bass, but it skipped these buds.
Oh, and these do not sound isolate, let alone noise cancel.
Good in some cases for situational awareness.
I would probably wear these to the gym, because of the comfort, you really can almost forget they're there.

Also the manuals on Viotek website seem to indicate that the GNV34DB has better RGB coverage (99% vs 96%) not sure how accurate this is but the GNV34DB appears to be the superior and newer product and its also weirdly cheaper.

First off the monitor needs to be calibrated, calibrating this monitor drastically improved the color and contrast.
Make sure you go into the setting on the monitor and check that everything is currently set.

I used lagom website's calibration test to calibrate gamma and contrast and ended up with 100 brightness and 70 contrast for around 2.2 gamma, using the contrast test color banding looks excellent after adjusting each rgb channel gamma using windows calibration.

Calibrating the display using just your eyesight should produce a decent result , but if you need more accuracy you will need to buy a calibration tool.

Finally, i think this monitor is beautiful (see attached pictures) i saw some other reviews from people saying the display looked washed out or the colors were off, maybe they had a bad display or it needed to be calibrated?

Easy setup and works well tldr: This is a great router.
It is very cheap for what you get.
If it lasts a year it will have paid for itself by not renting one from an ISP.
Signal is ok, could be stronger.

Don't buy unless your wifi can already take advantage of at least 802.11ac, and preferably ax to get the most out of it.

Buying our own router instead renting from the ISP saves about $10 to $15 per month, so they have a tendency to pay for themselves if you choose wisely.
We had an Archer C7 router for about 6 years that I paid about $100 for and although it worked great overall it was starting to show its age a little too much.

When the time came to upgrade I looked for an ax router to future proof our home network for a while and was hoping to find something in the same price band.

For an ax router in this price band the pickings were slim.
I ultimately chose this one because (a) it was the cheapest option, and (b) it had good reviews.

So far I am very happy with the selection.

It was very easy to set up out of the box.
In a ~2600 sq ft three level townhouse with the router on the middle floor we get signal throughout, although the 5 ghz band is weak upstairs and on the far side from the router.
The Archer C7 5 ghz band didn't reach there consistently, though, so at least now there's access.
Previously, I had to use the 2.4 ghz band and was getting about 2 Mb/s over usb wifi using 802.11n.
A combination of this router, an ax-capable PCI-E wifi card, and being able to get a 5 ghz signal means I now get about 80 Mb/s on the same computer, which caps out what the ISP will give me.

The difference is night and day.

So far, any issues I have would be nitpicking.
I wish the 5 ghz signal were just a little stronger and the router's interface is merely functional which means it could be cooler to interact with.

I personally am very happy that it just has one small LED indicator light on the front instead of the nearly dozen flashing icons on the Archer, but I guess some other people might prefer it the other way.
I had to get a new wifi receiver for the computer to take advantage of the 802.11ax standard, but that was something I knew going into this.

Very handy and reliable device I've held off writing this for a few days so I could make sure my review includes at least a few days worth of pretty heavy use.

So far, it has performed very well and met pretty much all of my expectations after several hours of use.

First of all, I was careful to follow the instructions for first use, including charging the unit fully (at least 2 hours) before using.

Once fully charged, I followed the instructions for powering on and pairing.
The instructions were clear and simple and the unit paired successfully with my Bose QC35 headphones in seconds.

It reconnects to the headphones without trouble every time I turn it on.

So far I have only used it as a transmitter, not a receiver, but it has worked great transmitting from my PC, my audio interface (home recording studio gear) and my stereo receiver for my home entertainment system.

In all cases, the audio is clear, powerful and nearly free of lag.

I say "nearly free of lag" because there does appear to be a few milliseconds of lag for video (YouTube, TV, etc.), but it's almost imperceptible unless you're really fixating on it and I find that my brain seems to compensate for it quickly to the point that I don't even really notice it anymore.
It is not distracting for me and has no effect on my enjoyment of whatever it is I'm watching.

Naturally, lag has no effect on listening to music or other audio only sources.

I have also noticed the sound cut out once or twice at very low volumes, but it was really quite low and even then it only cut for a second.

It's not something I would consider to be a problem or a defect.

As far as build quality, the unit is very small and very light, not much heft to it, but it does not feel "cheap."
It feels very tight and sturdy, the button feels substantial enough that I'm not afraid of it breaking under my thumb.
The unit has a really cool almost velvety surface texture to it as well, which lends an air of quality to it.

For its size and for the price, I have to admit to being rather impressed with the look and feel of it.

So far, I'm very pleased.
I'll give it a bit more time and use to be sure, but I will likely end up buying a few more.

As a user of the former Ubit Wifi 5 Bluetooth Card, this Installation was a breeze.
I installed it in place of my Wifi 5 card and shut up my system and booted it up.

There were no drivers to install or software changes to be made.

Further testing was done in order to see how much faster the Wifi 6 card really in a Wifi 5 LAN environment.
After 10 or 12 tests, I was very impressed.

Got more speed that I thought I would since the receiver was a Surface Pro 4 laptop that was obviously Wifi 5.

First I tested with the old Wifi5 card for a base measurement.

My test file was a 341,270 K file in all cases.

Wifi 5 to Wifi 5 Average 66.3 seconds to send file = 5147 KB/second

Wifi 6 to Wifi 5 Average 52 seconds to send file = 6563 KB/second (27% faster)

GB Ethernet to Wifi 5 Average 30 seconds to send file = 11,375 KB/second

I didn't test the Bluetooth performance since both cards were Bluetooth 5.0.

I'd really like to see the difference if BOTH ends were Wifi 6 but I don't have another Desktop and card to test with.
I'm very sure the tests would be better than all of the above.

Firstly, any new headphones will take a good few hours of listening for your ears to "adjust" to them, so keep that in mind.
I love their neutral audio balance.
The bass is definitely there and you hear it clearly and audibly, but it's not going to kick you in the head.

The neutral balance is unique to Bowers & Wilkins in the way that you can hear the entire range of audio, no matter what style of music you listen to (and trust me, I listen to a healthy amount of rock, metal, and electronic styles).

Next, along with the neutral audio balance, the positioning of the sound stage is superior to the competition.

The drivers are pointed forward at about 30-45 degrees, so it sounds like your face is right in front of a speaker and the sound comes from right in front of you, then forms around your head and into your ears.

At least, that's what it sounds like to me after my ears adjusted.

The only set-back is the microphone on these.
Yes, you can take phone calls using the Bluetooth features, but good luck trying to get your friends to understand what you're saying.

It's best to use these strictly as an audio listening device, forget the phone call features.

Apart from the lack of microphone functionality, the REST OF THE FUNCTIONS ARE INCREDIBLE for these headphones.
They know (most of the time) when they're being taken off or onto your head and over your years, they'll pause the music when one or both of the ear cups are not on your ears.
They come with a USB cable that serves not only as a charger, but also WORKS ON PS4 (and maybe other gaming consoles?)
AS A USB AUDIO DEVICE!

Furthermore, my favorite part, they come with a 3.5mm-3.5.mm cable to use as direct line-in audio for those of you that want to hear it through your fancy Quad-HD HiFi DAC device.

Noise-cancellation is pretty darn good, but could use a little improvement.
I work in a noisy office and when I put these on High ANC I can barely hear the loud chatter and clicking of keyboards & mice.

However, I think the Active Noise Cancellation is still not up-to-par to completely cancel-out the decibels of walking down a busy city sidewalk.

Lastly, but equally important to the rest of why this got a 4-star review, the BUILD QUALITY IS A HUGE IMPROVEMENT FROM PREVIOUS GENERATIONS.
The leather material on the ear cups is soft, comfortable, and doesn't press against the top of my jaw line like the P9 headphones.
The leather ear cups are removable and replaceable if they wear-out or get damaged.
The PX7s are durable, made with brushed carbon fiber (same material that you'll see on Ferrari or Lambourghini cars in some cases).
Despite their weight/mass, they feel lighter than they are, which gives a boost to their comfortability rating.

Don't rely on this I previously reviewed this product, and said that it was a really good buy.
But in fact, I've changed my mind with time.
The problem, I've found, was that once power is actually pulled, they don't hold up voltage levels.
This morning, power flickered here.
We're talking < 2 secs.
No big deal, but my computer was off when I came down to use it.
This was not the first time.
As long as it was down, I took a few minutes to test the battery.
I unplugged everything else from the battery ports, and connected a voltmeter.
Power output registered at about 120V, which is perfectly fine.
Then I pulled the power plug from it, and watched as the voltage level dropped down to a variable output of between 98V and 105V.
And that's why my computer is losing power.
But that's not why I wanted a battery backup unit.
I've had this unit since March.
Didn't expect it to last forever, but also didn't expect it to never quite have worked properly.

Serves me right for not testing it right early.

In any event, if you're looking for a surge protector, this one is fine, but you can get cheaper ones that'll work just as well.
If you're actually looking for a battery backup that will keep your devices up during brief power events, don't rely on it.

Defective telescope out of the box. 2nd Celestron with missing parts advertised as included I originally purchased a Celestron LCM80 for a family Christmas gift at a hobby shop about an hour from where we live.
We got it out of the box and it was missing the software download and the finderscope.
It was disappointing seeing how our kids went from being excited over their new Christmas gift to being sad that it didnt work.
I took it back to the hobby shop and got my money back as they didn't have a replacement and we didn't want to wait on getting the parts from Celestron.
I went to order a replacement on Amazon and the price we paid at the hobby shop was slightly less than the Nexstar 4Se offered by Amazon.
I did some research and the Nexstar 4Se seemed to be a better telescope than the LCM80 and it also included the rs232 cable to connect to our laptop for additional control.
This really sweetened the deal since the LCM80 did not include a rs232 computer cable.

We just had to purchase a rs232 to USB converter cable for $15.

About a week later we were excited to get our new NexStar 4SE.
We got it out of the box and inventoried the parts.
We got the finderscope and software download this time but there was no rs232 cable.
The getting started manual showed the rs232 cable should be included.
I contacted Celestron and they said the new on-board computer doesn't require an rs232 but does require a straight through USB cable so they quit including them.
So now we are short of a computer communications cable and we purchased a USB converter cable for the rs232 that is now useless.
After looking at some other amazon reviews for this product it is apparent Amazon knows this cable is not included yet they still advertise that it is included.

This is deceptive and they should change the description of the included items.

We got the scope mounted on the base and went to align the finderscope with the telescope and couldn't see any light being reflected into the eyepiece.
We followed the quick start guide and rotated the flip mirror control and still no light coming into the eye piece.
I looked inside the OTA and was unable to see a mirror.
I contacted Celestron and was told that this is very rare but the mirror is only held in place by a piece of double sided tape and something might have damaged it during the manufacturing process.
It doesn't sound like the mirror is loose in the OTA but instead may have never got installed (there is no visible tape residue on the plastic piece that supports the mirror) at the factory.
They suggested I send it back to Amazon as it was clearly defective.
After reviewing other Amazon posts for this telescope it looks like this problem might  be a frequent occurrence.
I am sending this one back and am hoping we get a working telescope that includes all the parts listed on Amazon's site.
I will post an update after getting a working unit.

This camera, by far, is the worst camera I have had after trying Wyze, Blink, and Canary.
I thought because of some of the reviews on Amazon as well as some of the reviews on websites through Google that the camera would meet an average expectation of security.
However, it has not!
I own a medical business that requires security and surveillance at all times.
Ring is limited in its ability to pick up on traffic going through my hallway because of its inability to pick up on motion from a distance.
A lot of the people coming in and out of my practice were not picked up on by this camera because of the short distance that it records.

The other issue with ring is that I had a 60-day subscription free trial and after it ended I lost ALL of my footage that I had wanted to save and transfer to a USB drive.

Most of the surveillance is extraordinarily important in my practice and if I don't have it that poses an issue.

Ring's unsophisticated subscription service disposed of all of my videos because it wasn't on the cloud when the subscription ended.

I don't see this as a good product because if there were hardcore evidence on that camera that I needed to prove something or to protect my business, I would not have it any longer.

I should not be forced to purchase a subscription (and purchase it immediately before my free trial ends so I don't lose my video storage) after paying $100 for a camera that I believe should provide recorded "copies" of all videos for free.

I returned this unsophisticated device to the store and I will NOT be purchasing or recommending another Ring device.

The device claims that it can be used for businesses but I HIGHLY discourage this.

I have five Canary cameras and I went and bought the sixth one after I return Ring.

Although not perfect, I feel that Canary at least provides the security that I need in my business.

Highly dissatisfied with the Ring product.

Beyond setup, prints are having issues with adhesion to the build plate, despite my using the included glue stick and the hair spray recommended by another reviewer.

It's a little lost and lonely at the moment though.

==== UPDATE: A COUPLE WEEKS LATER ====

After about 75 hours of printing, my problems got a lot worse and was unable to print anything, nothing would stick to the build plate at all.

I tried switching to a new filament and went from bad to worse.

I finally reached Tang for support and he was very responsive and helpful.
As a 3D printing novice I needed some help assessing the issues and Tang provided that and more.

Most helpful was a video demonstrating disassembly of the extruder which helped me identify a rookie mistake I made unloading the filament, resulting in a completely blocked filament tube.

As to my print quality and adhesion issues, those were maintenance related.
I had not kept the print nozzle clean enough and (worse) had cleaned it in a way that damaged it.

I ordered two nickle plated replacement nozzles (recommended) and a PLA solvent (Ethyl Acetate) for gentle cleaning.

Presently, I am printing again with eSUN PLA Pro filament which is fantastic and am very pleased with the prints.
The printer is simple to use and, once you get familiar with its needs, performs very well hour after hour.
I used to order prints through an online service and this printer has already paid for itself.

Feature Rich, Budget Friendly This Television was a holiday gift for the family - an upgrade from an older, smaller set that was starting to show its age.
For its size, this set was very reasonably priced - not the best deal out there, but the cheaper options all had fatal flaws.
The feature set is solid, the picture quality quite good and with an effective 120 Hz refresh rate, it's bright and responsive.
Color saturation is good with minimal or no bleedover, even when contrast is high.
Audio quality is surprisingly good for a flat screen, and can be very loud.
There is some distortion at high volume, but not anything really noticeable at any volume you might consider comfortable.
Set-up is easy, if somewhat tedious as the unit had to download and install three iterations of updates before it declared itself ready.

It's currently connected to our network using its built in wifi, but it also has an ethernet port for a faster, more robust connection if desired.

Ports are plentiful - there are four HDMI inputs, one USB Type A port and the above mentioned ethernet.
You can also connect coax or conventional Composite video sources, though I don't know anyone that uses such things anymore.
The set is Alexa compatible, though you will require an Alexa device to use that feature.
This was important to me - the set has neither Alexa nor Google Assistant built in - if it had, I would not have bought it.
The set is also compatible with Apple's Home Kit - a somewhat harder feature to find, but one that appealed to me since our family is invested in the Apple ecosystem.

Whatever your choice of digital assistants, though, this TV will likely work with it.

The remote is fairly comprehensive - but somewhat awkwardly laid out.
The most common controls used in our household (most notably the input select) are not as well placed as they might be, but that is a small complaint.
Build quality seems good - the supplied feet are metal, easy to install and fasten securely.
The set is also VESA mount compatible for those that wish to wall mount it.

Good cable management is a must to keep things tidy and the various connections easy to trace.

A few caveats - be sure to check the packaging - the first unit that I ordered arrived damaged - the box had been struck fairly hard and the frame of the set was bent and the screen badly cracked.

A return/exchange was easily set up on the web - the new set arrived just a few days later, and was in perfect condition.

As for the set itself, the on board software required updating during set up - it took while but was a straightforward procedure.
The Netflix app on the set crashed a few times, and getting it to operate correctly required a reboot of the TV.
Apple Airplay works well, but again, we had a lock up that required a reboot to correct.

That has only happened once so far, though so I do not consider it to be serious issue - if that changes, I'll update my review.

Bottom line - for the money, this set is hard to beat.
You can get a much better set, of course, but you'll pay correspondingly higher prices - and this unit does everything I want a TV set to do, and does it well.
If you're in the market for a good TV set and you haven't got a lot to spend, you'd have a hard time finding better.

Sound design, no pun intended This is a well designed push-pull power amplifier.
Going with the a dual rail 45Volt supply will yield the 100 Watts as advertised.
The power transistors are top notch and the drivers are on a nice size heat sink.
Make sure you use a decent size heat sink for the power transistors, say at least a 5" x 5", per pair.

I am going to mount them on a 12" x 5" x 1.3" Wakefield Vette aluminum fined Heat Sink, about $35 bucks from "Mo***er" Design a nice power supply or buy a
good linear one that will deliver at least 4 amps.
Stay away from switching supplies for audio stuff.
I know that sounds old school, but it is correct.
I am an EE.
Also you should shield the power supply from the amp proper, or even better put it into its own steel enclosure.
Then use a circular Amphenol connector to run the cables to the amp enclosure.
Amphenol part PT02E-10-6P(072) and Amphenol part PT06A-10-6P(072) will do.
These are 6 pin, you only really need 3, but this way you have extra conductors for fans and such that would reside in the amp proper enclosure.

Use the 5th and 6th wire for the fan drive and use the 6th as the ground, that is attached to the chassis of the power supply enclosure with a wire connecting the power supply enclosure to the amp proper enclosure.
This way each of the amp supply rails will have a floating supply.
If you do it this way, use some good 6 conductor sheilded cable, with 18 AWG stranded wire and tie the sheilding on the Power supply end to the chassis.

I make my own cables using good Mil spec PTFE insulated wire and a metal braided sleeve capturing the ends where the connectors attach with heat shrink.

Also use a stand by switch that goes in the center tap line of the transformer ( a good toroid), and place a 450R, 5 Watt resistor (Ohmite 45F450E) across the switch with a 0.1/630V Cap in parallel to reduce in rush current.
When you first turn to power supply on, wait for about 30 seconds before you close the stand by.
This will give the amp and power supply components a little bit to heat up, and reduce the inrush current.
When these components are cold, they have much lower resistance than when hot, on the order of a magnitude.
The 450R resistors allows approx. 100mA of current to be delivered; heating things up a bit.
This will increase longevity of all the components especially the toroid and power supply devices.

Also I would use fast diodes in the rectifier or use a bridge and then place one fast diode on each power rail right after the bridge; user a 30ns device that is say 600V at 10 amps
(ROHM RFN10TF6SFHC9).
I would cut the Wakefield Vette HS 125403 in half midway and mount each board to one the orient them so the fins face each other in the middle with about 2 inches betwen them.
Place a fan on the under side of the top of the enclosure, one at each end, and two in the middle; that have at least 100 cfm capacity.

When designing your supply, you can add a L7824CV 3 terminal regulator with a TO-220 clip on HS to the output of the positive side, with a 0.1uF/250V PP Cap on either side of it and a 100uF/100V eCap after the one on the output side.
Each fan will draw at most 150mA if you select them right and use the 24Volts to drive them.
Use 12V fans and pair them wired in series and you will have a nice rig.

Fantastic addition to a mobile work station I received this monitor as a Christmas gift this year - I specifically asked for it.
I have not been disappointed so far!
The main reason I wanted the monitor was to maximize my efficiency and productivity when working from home.
I run multiple displays at work, so it's always been difficult to transition to a single laptop screen when working from home.
With this portable monitor I can just plug a single cord into my laptop and then I'm off to the races!
The picture quality is better than expected.
It's definitely a HD screen.
The images are crisp, everything is very readable, and the colors are vibrant.
I have been primarily using this with my Surface Pro X, so the screen size is almost the same size as my Surface's.
This is ideal and makes everything look very deliberate.
Additionally, the smaller screen size of this monitor is great for its' portability.

It very easily fits into a small laptop bag right alongside my Surface.

The folding stand/cover that it comes with is also great.
It protects the monitor's screen from possible scratches/debris.
It also functions properly as a stand.
It has two slots for different viewing angles The stand works as intended, steadily holding up the monitor in either position.
One of the big bonuses for the cover is how thin it is.

It adds a negligible amount of width to the monitor itself, and essentially no additional weight.
Another bonus is the cover is easily removed by unscrewing the two hand screws on the back.

It's also very easy to put it back on.

I've also been using the monitor as a small, portable Dex station.
To do this all I need is a USB-C Dex compatible HDMI converter.
All I have to do is plug the HDMI cord into the monitor, use a USB-C cord plugged into a wall adapter for power, and plug the Dex converter into my phone.

It's incredibly easy to do.
It's been great to actually be able to utilize the Dex capabilities of my phone with this monitor.
It basically lets me have a laptop at the tip of my fingers.

It's something I'd never really had the opportunity to explore until I got this monitor.

Overall this is a fantastic little gadget.
It's something I'd easily buy for myself, and am actually considering buying a second one.
I put a lot of thought into which portable monitor I asked for for Christmas, and price for quality this one is truly hard to beat.
I would heavily recommend this monitor to anyone who has a need for small second monitor that won't remain stationary.
